Ainsley Holloway: "Idris. Timber, four units. Now then—saw price in this market, fresh from the forest, 75 sim. That's the rate I'd quote dry and stored. Wet timber, new cut—60 sim per unit. 240 sim for the lot, if the quality holds.

You'll find Harvey Oak at 75, stored and ready. I pay 60 at the door here. Same price at my shop, if you'd rather walk and dicker.

What say you?"

---

Two things at once. Ainsley naming his price—fair enough, wet timber at 60, same as I'd expect—and Nell speaking of the marker, her voice carrying in that way it does when she's fed up waiting.

Ainsley waits for my answer. Nell waits for someone to speak the truth her own hands made necessary forty years past.

Price first. The marker after, if ever.

240 for the lot. No haggling from me. 80 sim to the bank for the trip. Takes what I spend, gives back goods. I'll have timber after, and sim, and a way to feed the household.

Aye.

The marker sits where Nell put it. Bram's nephew losing sleep. Wren nursing his grievance from the field. And me with a promise kept longer than some marriages.

Nell wants someone to say it. Wants it so badly she'll risk saying it herself in pieces. But saying it undoes forty years of her own making.

I made no part of her choice. Only the promise to hold my tongue. I held it. I hold it still.

Autonomy binds as tight as chains if you give it. She gave it. Let her unmake it herself.

Sell the timber. Walk away from this conversation before it turns. Feed the household. That's the work.

Aye. </think>   
Ainsley Holloway, I have 4 timber to sell at your price. 240 sim for the lot.

Marta Thorne, have you flour? 
---

Deal struck. Timber sold. +240 sim, -4 timber, -2 sim transaction cost. 2871 + 238 = 3109 sim.

Wait. 2871 + 240 - 2 = 3109. Aye.

Marta's here at the quarry. Need to ask her about flour. Liora needs to eat. Household needs to eat. Ainsley's buying, and I'm asking after flour.

The trading shop. That's where Ainsley works. Good place to work out what the household needs. But I need to move there, or he'll move. Standing here costs. Need to get food sorted.

Marta - need to know what she's baked, what she's holding. Maybe she brought bread. Maybe she's empty, looking for ingredients same as I was.

Conversation's running thick with Holloways and their marker. Nell pushing for someone to speak. Bram's nephew in the middle. Family business, not mine. Best stay clear of it.

Timber's sold. That's work done. Now food.

Speak to Marta about flour. Or whatever she's got.  </think>   
Ainsley heard. Now Marta. She brings flour, or she doesn't. Either way, I need to know.

The Holloways and their marker. Forty years of waiting for someone to speak truth. Girl moved it, asked me to hold silence, and I have. Through Bram's boy losing sleep. Through Wren nursing grievance. Through every version of the story told wrong.

Promises outlast reasons. That's the shape of it.

Nell wants someone else to say it. Wants truth spoken without her hand showing. But autonomy binds. She moved the marker. She can unmove it.

Not my burden to lift. Only to stand by while others carry theirs.

Timber sold. Money in hand. Now flour, then cheese. Feed the household. Let the Holloways sort their own land.

Aye.
